samples.summary: New shared walk leaves a near-identical sibling copy behind in the same file — `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl`
samples.evidence: `range-runs.ts` opens with "One shared walk over the text runs a `DocRange` covers" and editor.ts:2839 claims "One shared walk with the keyboard path ... and with `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s write". But `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` (editor.ts:1089-1193) still carries a byte-for-byte-equivalent copy of the traversal that was just deleted from `getRangeStyleSummary`: same `collectRunsInBlock` overlap test, same cell-rectangle branch, same `doc.getBlockIndex` dispatch, and the same body-only `layout.blockParentMap.get(...)` lookup (editor.ts:1163-1164) that this diff explicitly identifies as broken for header/footer table cells. samples.summary: `visitTable` recurses into nested tables but `Doc.applyInlineStyle` does not — the read set no longer equals the write set the module promises to mirror
samples.evidence: range-runs.ts's docstring states it mirrors "`Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s dispatch" so "the runs read are the runs written". `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:63-79) recurses when `cellBlock.type === 'table'`; `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s table branch (document.ts:415-428) iterates only the cell's direct blocks and skips any with `getBlockTextLength === 0`, i.e. it never descends into a nested table. For a cross-block selection containing a table that itself contains a nested table (a supported feature — docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md), the read can report 'mixed'/`false` from runs the write will not touch, so a toggle can again be unable to reach a stable state — the same failure mode as #715.

verdict.reason: The claimed duplicate walk exists exactly as described. range-runs.ts:1-20 declares itself the "one shared walk" mirroring Doc.applyInlineStyle, and editor.ts:2839-2858 migrated getRangeStyleSummary to visitStyledRunsInRange (its comment explicitly names the body-only layout.blockParentMap lookup as unable to resolve header/footer table cells). Yet stepSelectionFontSizeImpl (editor.ts:1089-1193) still hand-rolls the same traversal: identical run-overlap test (1111-1125 vs range-runs.ts:54-62), identical cell-rectangle branch (1128-1146 vs range-runs.ts:86-101), the same getBlockIndex/getContextBlocks cross-block walk (1148-1161), the same same-cell multi-block branch (1165-1186), and it still uses the body-only layout.blockParentMap at 1163-1164; it also lacks any visitTable equivalent (range-runs.ts:68-83,164-167). The divergence is user-visible for the same style key: the toolbar reads fontSize from getRangeStyleSummary (use-resolved-font-size.ts:23,35,39-40) but writes it via stepSelectionFontSize (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:368), so the read and write now traverse different run sets. I weighed refuting as out-of-scope (the #715 task doc lists only B/I/U/S toggle work, font stepping is #343), but the summary-driven font-size read is coupled to the migrated walk, so the duplication/divergence is not confined to untouched unrelated code. Uncertainty keeps the finding.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. text-box-editor.ts:1017-1129 contains a third, un-migrated copy of the range summary walk (KEYS :1044, tokenize :1059, visitInlinesInBlock :1067) that reads the raw `inline.style` at :1077 with no `resolveStyleInline` defaults, while the shared walk it should reuse (range-runs.ts:52,58) explicitly layers named-style inline defaults. The keyboard path this change adds — TextEditor.toggleStyle :2895 -> isStyleOnInSelection :3007-3019 -> visitStyledRunsInRange — does layer them, and the slides text-box editor constructs that very TextEditor (text-box-editor.ts:666), so Cmd+B/I/U on a slides text box uses defaults-aware reads while the slides mobile toolbar (mobile-toolbar.tsx:229-243, which reads the text-box getRangeStyleSummary for both pressed state and the applied value) does not. The divergence is reachable, not hypothetical: blockStyleId derives the style from block.type (named-styles.ts:99-114) and BUILTIN_STYLES['heading-6'] sets italic:true (named-styles.ts:91), and the text-box API exposes setBlockType with headingLevel (text-box-editor.ts:277,291,1172). Under the design-fit rubric this is major on two counts: it duplicates the now-canonical range-runs.ts module instead of reusing it, and it fails the change's own stated premise/acceptance (docs/tasks/active/20260810-docs-range-aware-toggles-todo.md:29-34 asserts both editors share the "same caret walk, same named-style defaults"; :49-57 makes toolbar/keyboard agreement including the slides mobile bar a deliverable). No guard elsewhere neutralizes it and it is squarely in this lens's lane.

finding.summary: `visitTable` recurses into nested tables but `Doc.applyInlineStyle` does not — the read set no longer equals the write set the module promises to mirror
finding.evidence: range-runs.ts's docstring states it mirrors "`Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s dispatch" so "the runs read are the runs written". `visitTable` (range-runs.ts:63-79) recurses when `cellBlock.type === 'table'`; `Doc.applyInlineStyle`'s table branch (document.ts:415-428) iterates only the cell's direct blocks and skips any with `getBlockTextLength === 0`, i.e. it never descends into a nested table. For a cross-block selection containing a table that itself contains a nested table (a supported feature — docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md), the read can report 'mixed'/`false` from runs the write will not touch, so a toggle can again be unable to reach a stable state — the same failure mode as #715.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. range-runs.ts:74-79 recurses into nested table blocks (`visitTable(cellBlock)`), and range-runs.ts:162-167 routes cross-block table blocks through `visitTable`. Doc.applyInlineStyle's table branch (document.ts:415-428) only iterates `cell.blocks` and calls `store.applyStyle` when `getBlockTextLength(cellBlock) > 0`; since getBlockTextLength (types.ts:326-328) sums only `block.inlines`, a nested table block measures 0 and is skipped with no recursion — so the write never touches nested-table content the read reports on. This breaks the invariant the module explicitly promises (range-runs.ts:8-10, 42: "the runs read are the runs written"), which is the basis of the #715 fix. It is reachable: nested tables are a supported feature with an editor insertion path (Document.insertTableInCell, tested in packages/docs/test/model/nested-table.test.ts) and docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:20-22 lists styling parity inside nested tables as a Goal, not a Non-Goal. Consumers act on the read directly (text-editor.ts:3007-3019 isStyleOnInSelection sets allOn=false for any unstyled visited run; editor.ts:2849 for the toolbar), so a selection containing a nested table can read "not applied" indefinitely while the write cannot change those runs. No guard elsewhere excludes nested tables from either path, so none of not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope applies.

finding.summary: Keyboard range read omits named-style inline defaults, so keyboard and toolbar can still disagree — the acceptance goal of the fix
finding.evidence: `isStyleOnInSelection` tests `(inline.style as Record<string, unknown>)[key]` only. `getRangeStyleSummary` (editor.ts:2847 / :2791) layers `styleDefaultsForBlock(block)` = `resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), doc.document.styles)` under each run, and named styles can carry `bold` (see `packages/docs/test/model/named-styles.test.ts:97`: `resolveStyleInline('heading-1', docStyles)` → `{ fontSize: 28, bold: true }`). On such a block with no explicit run bold, the toolbar reports on → click removes, while Cmd+B computes off → applies bold. The todo's stated outcome ("Without it the keyboard and the fixed toolbar disagreed on the same selection") is therefore only partially met.

verdict.reason: The claim is that the keyboard range read (`isStyleOnInSelection`) omits named-style inline defaults that the toolbar's `getRangeStyleSummary` applies. The code shows the opposite. `isStyleOnInSelection` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3007-3019) does NOT read `inline.style`; it delegates to `visitStyledRunsInRange(this.doc, range, (style) => ...)` and tests the visitor's first argument. In packages/docs/src/view/range-runs.ts:52 that walk computes `const defaults = resolveStyleInline(blockStyleId(block), doc.document.styles)` and at :58 reports each run as `{ ...defaults, ...inline.style }` — i.e. named-style inline defaults layered underneath, exactly the layering the finding says is missing (documented at range-runs.ts:12-16, and again in the method docstring at text-editor.ts:2998-3002). The toolbar path uses the identical walk: editor.ts:2849 `visitStyledRunsInRange(doc, range, (effective) => ...)`, with the comment at editor.ts:2839-2848 stating it is one shared walk with `TextEditor`'s `isStyleOnInSelection` and that each run carries its named-style defaults. On a `heading-1` block with no explicit run bold both paths therefore see `bold: true` from the same merged object, so the described keyboard/toolbar divergence cannot occur through this route. The reviewer's quoted evidence (`(inline.style as Record<string, unknown>)[key]`) does not appear in the function; their search list missed the indirection through range-runs.ts.
